text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 0.45% today, extending a sharp decline over the past week that has wiped out most of its two-week gains. The decline fits a broader pullback in oil refining stocks despite crude prices staying elevated—Brent crude is near six-month highs above $116 per barrel due to Middle East tensions and Iran concerns. However, U.S. refinery utilization has slipped to 93.4%, and gasoline and diesel inventories remain relatively high, which can pressure refiner margins by reducing urgency for new production.

The recent news cycle has been dominated by geopolitical risk—Iranian-backed Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites, U.S. threats of military action against Iran, and concerns about oil market manipulation. While these headlines have pushed crude prices up, refiner profitability depends on the *spread* between crude input costs and the value of finished fuels like gasoline and diesel; high crude prices without corresponding fuel demand can actually squeeze margins, which appears to be weighing on the stock despite the headline oil price strength.
